payload.claim: The call to `package_phase.reverify` omits `exempt`, so it defaults to `()` (`saffron/phases/package.py:491`). `exempt` is how PACKAGE carries forward `outcome.revert_exempt` (`saffron/cell/session.py:3457`, `saffron/phases/package.py:843`), the set of new test names a post-rebuttal probe confirmed guard a property already true at base, which `revert_gate` must not fail even though they are new (`saffron/gates/core/revert.py:131-135`, comment at 390: "a rebuttal test that kills one can guard a property already true at base, so `revert` spares it"). Because this list is never persisted to the ledger (no column or fact holds it) and `regate.py` does not reconstruct it, any task whose original PACKAGE run earned such an exemption will have that same test re-evaluated by `revert` with no exemption during `regate`, and can now fail as theater even though the identical gate suite judged it fine at package time. This makes `regate`'s new-failure count and exit code wrong for exactly the tasks this mechanism exists for, which gates and the accompanying tests (which never assert anything about `exempt`) cannot see.
